title: Means, exchange, and completion
japaneseTitle: みんなの日本語 第7課
summary: Say how or in which language something is done, track who gives and receives, and ask whether an action is already complete.
sourceFiles: みんなの日本語　第7課.pdf
takeaways: で marks a tool, method, or language used to perform an action.
あげます points away from the giver; もらいます frames the event from the receiver.
もう + past asks or says “already”; a negative reply is まだです.

grammar.title: Name the means or language
grammar.summary: Use で after the tool, method, service, or language through which an action is carried out.

examples.english: I write academic papers in English.

grammar.caution: The same で marks where an action happens and what enables it. Read the noun and the action to decide whether it names the scene or the means.

grammar.title: Track the direction of an exchange
grammar.pattern: Person に Noun を あげます／Person に・から Noun を もらいます
grammar.summary: With あげます, に marks the recipient. With もらいます, に or から marks the person from whom the receiver gets something.

examples.english: I received a book from a friend.

grammar.caution: Choose the verb from the sentence viewpoint: あげます follows the thing from giver to recipient; もらいます describes the receiver obtaining it.

grammar.title: Check whether it is done
grammar.pattern: もう Verb ましたか → はい、もう Verb ました／いいえ、まだです
grammar.summary: Put もう before a past verb to ask or say that an expected action is already complete. Answer まだです when it is not complete yet.
grammar.caution: For the short negative reply, use まだです. Do not answer もう + a negative verb when you mean “not yet.”

recall.prompt: How do you ask “What is ‘thank you’ in Japanese?”
recall.answer: 「Thank you」は[[日本語|にほんご]]で[[何|なん]]ですか。

recall.prompt: Which particle marks the recipient with あげます?
How do you answer もう[[食べましたか|たべましたか]] if you have not eaten yet?
